title: I'm building a jet ski combat racing game using AI tools and Unreal Engine 5. Here's the actual gameplay!
author: Ok-Ad3563
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I've been experimenting with how far AI can take game development, and I wanted to share the results of a project I've been working on called WAVE RAGE.

The concept is basically Road Rash, but with jet skis. High-speed water racing where you can punch opponents, use melee weapons, collect nitro boosts, launch off ramps, and deal with unexpected hazards.

I'm developing it as a solo project using a combination of AI tools and traditional game development software.

Tools I've been using:

* Unreal Engine 5: The main game engine, including environments, gameplay, physics, and rendering.
* Claude Fable: AI-assisted development, coding, and system integration.
* Meshy AI: Generating 3D models and assets.
* Blender: Preparing models, rigging characters, and working on animations.

The game currently features:

* Two racing environments: Ibiza and Dubai.
* Jet ski racing against AI opponents.
* Melee combat while racing.
* Nitro boosts, ramps, and jumps.
* Different playable characters.
* Environmental hazards and special events.

To be clear, this isn't an AI-generated cinematic or a concept video. The footage shows actual gameplay from the Unreal Engine project.

Is it perfect? Definitely not.

There's still plenty of room for improvement, especially with character animations, combat, physics, and general gameplay polish. Some things that seem simple, like making characters grip handlebars properly or keeping their feet positioned correctly, have been surprisingly difficult.

But that's part of the experiment. I wanted to see what one person could actually build by combining AI-assisted development with existing creative tools, rather than just generating impressive-looking images.

I recorded some gameplay so you can see the current state of the project.

**🎮 Full gameplay:**

[https://youtu.be/1eNolcHQ2HY](https://youtu.be/1eNolcHQ2HY)

I'd genuinely appreciate feedback from other developers and gamers.

What do you think of the concept? What stands out as needing the most improvement?

And more importantly, would you actually want to play something like this?

Thanks for checking it out!
